clauses.reason: Executive Order 11013, signed 1962-04-07 (27 FR 3373), creates under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 a Board of Inquiry of three named members to inquire into the issues in the maritime dispute described in its recitals, gives it the powers and duties set forth in Title II of that Act, directs it to report to the President "on or before April 11, 1962." and provides that upon submission of its report the Board continues in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the Act, "until the Board is terminated by the President." The order contains no standstill or status-quo provision. The report date is a deadline, not an end, and the actual report date is not shown by any held source. The only own-terms end is termination by the President; no held source records it, and it is disclosed as an open earlier-end candidate rather than claimed. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and" "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" Its table on page 12 of the held text prints this order as the one-line row "11013 Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the maritime industry", which agrees with the order's title. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective and take effect; the only hit is a word inside another order's subject line), so the signing date, 1986-02-25, is recorded; the filing date 1986-02-26 (the held text prints "Filed 2-26-86") and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 are the alternative readings, and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11013 (27 FR 3373, Federal Register of April 10, 1962), signed by John F. Kennedy and dated April 7, 1962; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: one whole-order clause covers the heading, the two recitals and the operative text, which is a Labor Management Relations Act, 1947, section 206 board of inquiry order with no Railway Labor Act content and no status-quo or standstill sentence. Its commands are: creation of a Board of Inquiry of three named members to inquire into the issues in the maritime dispute; the grant of the powers and duties set forth in Title II of that Act; the direction to report to the President on or before April 11, 1962; and the provision that upon submission of its report the Board continues in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the Act until the Board is terminated by the President. Ending: EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 revokes the order by number. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (two machine hits) are the revocation note on this order naming EO 12553 and the matching note on EO 12553. The held-text number-citation scan found the number only on the order's own Federal Register page.

savings.reason: After a bounded search of the full held text of EO 12553 (no savings clause or exception attached to the revocation list), the U.S. Code and eCFR searches (no hits for this order) and the Federal Register catalog notes, no surviving legal effect of the order was found; EO 12553 revokes it without reservation.
